# 1 Clement Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 16

**16:1** For Christ is with the humble-minded, not with those who exalt themselves over his flock.

**16:2** The scepter of the majesty of God, the Lord Jesus Christ, did not come with the pomp of arrogance or overweening pride — though he might have done so — but in humility of mind, as the Holy Spirit spoke concerning him.

**16:3** For it says: "Lord, who believed our report, and to whom was the arm of the Lord revealed? We proclaimed before him as a child, as a root in thirsty ground; he has no form nor glory; and we saw him, and he had no form nor comeliness; but his form was dishonorable, inferior to men, a man in suffering, and accustomed to bearing sickness, because his face was turned away; he was dishonored and not esteemed." [Isa 53:1-3 LXX]

**16:4** "He bears our sins and is pained for us; and we regarded him as being in toil and suffering and affliction." [Isa 53:4 LXX]

**16:5** "But he was wounded for our transgressions, and he had been bruised because of our iniquities. The chastisement of our peace was upon him; by his bruises we were healed." [Isa 53:5 LXX]

**16:6** "All we as sheep went astray; each went astray in his own way; and the Lord delivered him up for our sins." [Isa 53:6 LXX]

**16:7** "And he, because of his affliction, opened not his mouth. As a sheep he was led to slaughter; and as a lamb before his shearer is silent, so opened he not his mouth." [Isa 53:7 LXX]

**16:8** "In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. His generation who shall declare? For his life is taken from the earth." [Isa 53:8 LXX]

**16:9** "Because of the transgressions of my people he was led to death." [Isa 53:8b LXX]

**16:10** "And I will give the wicked in return for his burial, and the rich in return for his death; because he did no lawlessness, and no deceit was found in his mouth." [Isa 53:9 LXX]

**16:11** "And the Lord wills to cleanse him from his suffering. If you make an offering for sin, your soul shall see a long-lived seed." [Isa 53:10 LXX]

**16:12** "He shall see light and be satisfied; and with his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many, and he shall bear their iniquities." [Isa 53:11 LXX]

**16:13** "Therefore he shall inherit many and divide the spoil of the strong, because his soul was delivered up to death, and he was reckoned among the transgressors; and he bore the sins of many, and because of their sins he was delivered up." [Isa 53:12 LXX]

**16:14** And again he himself says: "But I am a worm and not a man, a reproach of men and an outcast of the people. All who see me mocked me; they spoke with their lips, they shook their heads, saying, 'He hoped in the Lord; let him deliver him; let him save him, since he delights in him.'" [Ps 22:6-8 LXX]

**16:15** You see, beloved, what is the pattern set before us; for if the Lord was so humble-minded, what shall we do, who through him have come under the yoke of his grace?

---

*EMET: The fullest citation of Isaiah 53 in the Apostolic Fathers. This is Clement's Christological center. Isaiah 53 is read as a hymn to Christ's humility — the theological foundation for the humility he is demanding of the Corinthians.*
